input.description: Show store file and list repo files
Find callers of deleteRepo and admin context usage

input.command: cat -n src/routes.ts; cat -n src/git-auth.ts; cat -n src/config.ts; cat package.json

input.reason: I read src/store.ts, src/routes.ts, src/config.ts, src/git-auth.ts and package.json. In Store.deleteRepo, a caller whose isAdmin is false reaches line 29. That DELETE uses `owner = ? OR owner = 'system'`, so it also removes rows owned by `system` that the caller does not own. The only caller is the deleteRepo route at src/routes.ts:26-33, which passes req.user straight to store.deleteRepo with no role or ownership check of its own. There are no tests and no other guard. The finding holds, so I kept it unchanged.
input.summary: Non-admin users can delete system-owned repos via Store.deleteRepo

findings.text: For a non-admin caller the delete also matches rows whose owner is `system`, so any authenticated user can delete shared system repositories.
findings.reason: Claim 1: for a non-admin caller the delete also matches rows owned by `system`. This holds. When ctx.isAdmin is false, the admin branch at store.ts:25-28 is skipped, and line 29 runs `DELETE FROM repos WHERE id = ? AND (owner = ? OR owner = 'system')`. That matches rows owned by the caller's oid and also rows owned by 'system'. Claim 2: any authenticated user can delete shared system repositories. This also holds. The route handler at routes.ts:26-33 calls `store.deleteRepo(req.params.id, req.user)` with the request's UserContext and does no extra authorization. Any user who is not an admin reaches line 29 and can delete a system-owned repo by its id. The delete succeeds because result.changes is greater than 0, and the route returns 204. I found no test or other code that blocks this.

evidence.code: const result = await this.db.run("DELETE FROM repos WHERE id = ? AND (owner = ? OR owner = 'system')", [id, ctx.oid]);

input.severity_reason: This is an exploitable broken access control flaw. Any authenticated user who is not an admin can permanently delete shared system-owned repository records through the public deleteRepo route, and nothing else checks permission first. The result is unauthorized data loss.
